searchText: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/3312 I think that's acceptable, but 🤷 <@689161464829050960> What are your thoughts on `CALL_FROM` as the opcode name? it breaks the `*CALL` scheme though 😦 `FROMCALL`? 😬 `SPONSOREDCALL`? `IMPERSONATEDCALL`? we came up with a couple: `TXCALL` `SIGNEDCALL` `TXCALL` is what is currently in the EIP. I'm not a fan of it personally, as I don't think it accurately captures what it is doing. i agree, not quite a tx `SIGNEDCALL` I like more, but I still feel it isn't a *great* description of the *what*, but rather a description of the *how*. I generally think functions should be named after their *what* not their *how*. (and opcodes are like little tiny functions) `IMITATECALL` This is most certainly not a hill I want to die on, or even spend a large amount of time fighting on. I would just prefer to come up with a name that indicates *what* this does rather than *how* it does it. I think `IMPERSONATE` is used more often in software for this purpose than imitate. `CALLAS` and `CALLFROM` are the best IMO if it were not for breaking the naming convention Both imitate/impersonate I think are basically the same though. i went to the thesaurus result for impersonate 😄 I like `IMPERSONATECALL` the best so far. Or `CALLAS` if we are willing to break the convention. we would be stealing `IMPERSONATECALL` from 2997 (not that it's a very big deal) maybe we float `CALLAS` to broader community? Are we allowed to use underscores? 😬 `CALL_AS` i mean, if we're breaking conventions - why not! <@689161464829050960> Did you disagree with the additional changes I proposed in https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-3074-sponsored-transaction-precompile/4880/5, or have you just not yet had a chance to read about/think about/integrate them? If it is the latter, I would be curious to hear your arguments on the matter. Also, I have submitted two PRs related to some stuff we have discussed in here on 3074. My hope is to give us a place to catalog discussion and (if you ultimately agree) to make it easy to make the change. I forgot about the reordering, so I'll get to that. I really don't think we should remove chainID though. Can you remind me why, or better yet encode your reasoning in the magicians thread so I don't keep asking you. 😄 Sure thing! tl;dr is that I think chain-id agnostic invokers will be exceedingly rare. Is there a reason you think that contracts cannot implement replay handling logic? Or do you just think the EVM should be programmed to do that for the user? <@689161464829050960> Can you help me understand the `sponser != sponsee` check? What is the attack vector where a sponsor sponsors themselves? This one is my initial favorite, but might be overly specific RE: the "what" vs "how" The chain-id check can be implemented in the invoker, but it's gonna be in practically every invoker, no? If a contract currently assumes that `tx.origin == msg.sender` only happens in the top-level stack frame, they might rely on it for reentrancy protection. In my PR where I removed the changes to `ORIGIN`, I mentioned that I hated it but didn't like coupling the change of semantic meaning of `tx.origin`. However, I have zero problem breaking contracts that use it despite security experts and core developers telling them not to for half a decade. So my preference is to leave `ORIGIN` to still mean `ORIGIN`, but not create additional checks in the opcode execution to protect people who are doing things they were advised against doing. To put it another way, I don't think we should go out of our way at all to help people who have been using `tx.origin`. The primary use case for replayable transactions is one-time contract deployments. Though, thinking more on this I guess this cannot be used for sponsored deployments since we don't do a `CREATE` in the case where `to == 0`? Yeah, you'd have to call into a standardized deployer contract to do it. Do we *want* to enable sponsored contract deployments? `if (to == 0) create(...) else call(...)` <@!415548822983278593> was arguing for that as well. `CALL` doesn't create a new contract, so for consistency, I think we shouldn't do that. And you _can_ still create contracts, just less ideally. I think the only thing that I'm undecided on is returning gas used. (took `valueSponseeMax` back out since it has weird mempool implications) Meaning you cannot send value to the sponsored transaction from the sponsee? FWIW I'm still pretty against this. It doesn't align with how any CALL opcodes behave and we don't have a good place to put it that doesn't totally change the behavior of how call semantics works. Exactly. Any value has to come from the invoker. We can put it on the stack, no? Much easier as an opcode. Oh, so you still can pass value along? is the reason for gas used incase gas becomes unobservable? Yes Exactly. This would be a surprising behavior seeing as how none of the other CALL opcodes push more than just success boolean onto the stack. And I feel like adding gas observability in case we remove gas observability isn't a great argument. 🙂 We don't want to remove gas observability in a way that makes it still observable, we want to remove gas observability period. And force developers to come up with paradigms that don't require gas observability. gas observability is a requirement of sponsored txs We're already pushing two stack elements 😉 Hmm, really? What? I thought it was just the success/failure? *grumble* (found it) https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/EIPS/eip-3074.md#outputs `success` and `calleeSuccess` I'm against that for the same reason I was before. We should be returning a single success boolean and an appropriate revert reason. This particular flavor of gas observability is safe, so it shouldn't be a problem. No other opcodes set a revert reason though, and none of them modify a user supplied revert reason, afaik What prevents people from using `TXCALL` to gain access to gas observability? They could! But the contract can never reduce the amount of gas below what the EOA signed, so there's always a way for a human to set the gas limit. > No other opcodes set a revert reason though Perhaps they should. 🙂 Useful errors are useful. Consistent error mechanics are useful too. I'm getting quite tired (very late here), would you mind writing up your arguments for gas observability (why we want them, and why they aren't bad, and why it wouldn't create a way to get around gas observability removal) and also why you think two return values is better than one return value and a revert reason. I would like to continue to press on getting 3074 into a state everyone is happy with so it has a high chance of landing in Berlin, but I acknowledge that I'm below useful in a discussion at the moment. Perhaps on the discussions-to thread. I can do that, sure. I really appreciate your input!
